skill.name: project-domain
skill.description: Provides a template for capturing domain vocabulary, entity relationships, terminology rules, and model locations for a software project.
skill.summary: Keep project terminology, entities, and relationships consistent across code and documentation.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code formatting, and table headings in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe command execution evidence was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 47 starts a Markdown fenced block for an entity relationship example. It does not contain Ruby execution, shell execution, or user-controlled command construction.
Line 54 closes the Markdown fenced block shown above. The surrounding content is documentation text, not executable code.
The backticks on line 87 format the path src/models as inline Markdown code. No command is invoked and no external process is described.
Line 60 is a terminology table header for project vocabulary. It does not instruct the assistant to inspect host system details or perform reconnaissance.
Line 66 is a status fields table header for domain entities. It documents business state transitions and does not request system enumeration.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when models, APIs, and documentation use inconsistent business terms. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a shared domain glossary and relationship map.
actual_capabilities: Defines a structure for core domain entities and model locations.
Documents relationships between entities using a simple relationship section.
Records preferred terminology and terms to avoid.
Captures valid status values and allowed transitions.
Links domain rules to ORM models, BAML types, API schemas, and frontend types.
Gives assistants a checklist for terminology and relationship consistency.
limitations: The template ships with TODO placeholders that must be filled for each project.
It does not inspect source code or generate a glossary automatically.
It depends on maintainers to keep relationships and validation rules current.
It provides guidance, not runtime enforcement or schema validation.

use_cases.title: Align Domain Terms
use_cases.description: Create one reference for entity names, accepted terms, and terms that should not be used.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Changes
use_cases.description: Give coding assistants project-specific language before they edit models, APIs, or frontend types.

use_cases.title: Review Model Relationships
use_cases.description: Check that new fields, statuses, and relationships follow existing domain rules.

prompt_templates.title: Fill the Glossary
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-domain skill to draft glossary entries for the main entities in this project. Include definitions and model locations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project glossary

prompt_templates.title: Check Terminology
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed change with the project-domain skill. Flag inconsistent terms, duplicated concepts, and unclear entity names.

prompt_templates.title: Map Relationships
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-domain skill to describe relationships between the affected entities. Include cardinality, ownership, and important constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Domain Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the project-domain skill to audit this feature design. Compare entity names, statuses, transitions, validation rules, and model locations.

output_examples.input: Review the order status terms in this feature proposal.
output_examples.output: The review identifies preferred status names, notes two inconsistent synonyms, and recommends updating the proposal to match existing transitions.

output_examples.input: Create a domain summary for customer, subscription, and invoice entities.
output_examples.output: The summary lists each entity, its responsibility, related models, key relationships, and validation rules that should guide implementation.

output_examples.input: Check whether a new AccountProfile model duplicates existing concepts.
output_examples.output: The analysis compares the proposed model with the glossary and highlights overlapping fields, unclear ownership, and naming changes to consider.

best_practices: Replace all TODO placeholders before relying on the skill for project work.
Update the glossary whenever models, API schemas, or frontend types change.
Keep definitions short and link each entity to its primary source location.
anti_patterns: Using the template without adding project-specific entities or rules.
Adding synonyms that hide duplicate concepts instead of choosing one term.
Treating the skill as enforcement when validation still needs tests or schemas.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps assistants use consistent domain terms, relationships, statuses, and model locations while working on a software project.

faq.question: Does it generate the domain model automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides a template that maintainers must fill with project-specific entities, rules, and locations.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill during implementation?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code can use it as project context when reviewing or changing models, APIs, and frontend types.

faq.question: Can Codex use the same domain vocabulary?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can use the glossary and rules to keep code changes aligned with project terminology.

faq.question: Does the skill run external commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill is Markdown documentation and does not execute commands or scripts.

faq.question: How should teams maintain it?
faq.answer: Update it during model, schema, and business rule changes so assistants receive current domain context.
